consumer: The engine's detection/targeting eligibility logic asking 'can the avatar see this specific monster right now?', i.e. g->u.sees(mon) used to decide whether the monster is a valid detected/targetable creature.
scope: The avatar-versus-this-one-monster pair evaluated against the live map (LOS, light, range, concealment along the line between them) — not a window-filtered position snapshot.
decisive_source: src/creature.cpp::Creature::sees — computes a boolean by checking hallucination/dimension, range, light, line-of-sight via map::sees, and concealment/crouch/hide coverage, returning the engine's authoritative can-see verdict.
divergence: A monster inside the export window at close range but standing behind an opaque wall (or in darkness, or crouched-hidden): raw exported position says 'present', but Creature::sees returns false; re-deriving visibility from the exported position alone would falsely report it as seen.
